tldr: Continuing randomized feature experiments face a joint choice of daily allocation and borrowing when a transition model is approximate. For every fixed horizon, the note certifies the full-procedure minimax prediction risk \(R_T\) and shortest honest connected-interval length \(H_T\) for the realized latent running effect. A growing finite game retains the complete deterministic energy balls and all predictable allocation rules, supplies arbitrarily narrow rational brackets, and reconstructs point rules and exactly honest intervals. At zero transition-error radius the complete uniform limit is a sequence-design optimum, computable by finite graphs; a periodic schedule can beat every constant count. Aggregate borrowing already gives some honest gain at every finite radius. A common positive-radius horizon limit and its exact asymptotic amount of gain remain open. The Microsoft/Bing experimentation setting is a prospective consumer, not an empirical validation of this model.
gap: Shao, Wei and Wang give the closest state-space A/B formulation and a nominal constant-allocation spectral calculation. Sequential representation and bounded-Gaussian decision theory are available separately. The inspected sources do not give an all-design robust value approximation preserving a latent realized target, microscopic allocation words and every deterministic energy-bounded transition input.
